newsitem.title: NORWAY: World's first multipurpose tanker heads for Norway.
newsitem.headline: World's first multipurpose tanker heads for Norway.

text.p: The world's first multipurpose shuttle tanker (MST), Berge Hugin, was delivered last week to a partnership between Den norske stats oljeselskap AS and Bergesen ASA from its South Korean shipyard, Statoil's Status Weekly newsletter said on Thursday.
The vessel is sailing towards the North Sea as a conventional tanker and will pick up a cargo of oil from the Middle East or Europe on the way, Statoil said.
The company said it planned to use Berge Hugin as a production ship on Britain's Pierce field, which is due to begin producing on July 1, 1998.
The MST is initially due to spend five years at the British field but with options for extension. Operator of Pierce, British Petroleum, plans to seek government approval for the development in May.

Before start up of Pierce, Berge Hugin will be used as a shuttle tanker in the Norwegian North Sea and will serve as an unmoored storage ship during well testing on the Statoil-operated Connemara field off Ireland.
It also is scheduled to serve as a combined shuttle tanker and storage vessel on Statoil's Heidrun field off mid-Norway in the Norwegian Sea.
